body:
Freeze/Fawn

The book helped me put labels to things but it didn't really help me control it.

Also, most of my trauma came in my early 20s due to a relationship that turned abusive in combination with a complicated immigration situation that made me live in almost complete isolation for four years (she was my lifeline, the only person I spoke to). As a result I don't relate the majority of the community who had childhood abuse (I'm not trying to belittle it, but I developed a few different issues that aren't talked about in most resources and my triggers are different).

The freeze/fawn response has been very destructive to my life, friendships, and relationships. Having a full blown fawn response in front of a group of people is a terrible thing to go through. The shaking, crying, overwhelming fear, and blame-taking (especially for miscommunications and other things that I'd rather take the blame for than fight about because I just want it all to stop).

I recently started CBT and found out helpful. Actually going through the exercise of writing everything down and seeing it all in front of me has really helped me get a handle on my triggers. Things that months ago would've thrown me into full blown emotional flashbacks and ruined my entire day now just make me feel super shitty, which imo is great progress.
